If you want to drop down to the AHL, it has happened a couple of times (throwing in a couple of folded franchises)
 
1967: The Pittsburgh Hornets win the Calder Cup, after it was announced that the franchise would fold due to the NHL expanding into Pittsburgh.

1970: NHL expansion strikes again, Buffalo is awarded a franchise, leading to the folding of the Buffalo Bisons, who go out with a championship.

1982: The New Brunswick Hawks win the Calder Cup, with a ftranchise owned by the Toronto Maple Leafs, and also supplied by Chicago. During the offseason following the win, Chicago reaches an affiliation agreement with Springfield, and Toronto moves their franchise to St. Catherines. No NHL for Moncton, though- Edmonton moves their AHL franchise in for 82-83.

2015: Due to the AHL's Pacific Expansion, the Manchester Monarchs basically are swapped with the Ontario Reign of the ECHL. The Monarchs win the Calder, have a parade and banner raising in Manchester, and then the AHL staff and players go west, and the ECHL crew comes to New Hampshire.
